false_friends: Uruguay (same Río de la Plata region and grassland)

road_furniture.curb_style: Dense formal European-style street layout and kerbs in central Buenos Aires; open, minimal shoulders on rural Pampas roads.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Long straight rural roads across flat farmland outside the city.

architecture.roof_style: Ornate mansard and pitched roofs on Buenos Aires' Parisian-style apartment buildings; low-pitch tile/metal roofs on rural estancia ranch buildings.
architecture.roof_material: Slate/tile in central Buenos Aires' European-style buildings; corrugated metal on rural ranch structures.
architecture.wall_construction: Grand French/Italian/Spanish-influenced stone and stucco apartment buildings line Buenos Aires' boulevards; colourful corrugated-metal houses in La Boca; thick-walled adobe estancia ranch buildings out on the Pampas.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Elegant cream/grey European stone tones in central Buenos Aires; brightly painted corrugated houses in La Boca; earthy tones on rural estancias.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Parisian-style apartment blocks and grand boulevards (Avenida 9 de Julio); colourful La Boca houses; rustic estancia ranch buildings surrounded by flat grassland; grain silos and cattle fencing across the open Pampas.

nature.vegetation: Vast, flat, fertile grassland — the Pampas — used for cattle grazing and crop farming (soy, wheat, corn); very few trees except windbreaks and those planted near estancias.
nature.terrain: Extremely flat plains extending from Buenos Aires south to Bahía Blanca and west across the country's agricultural heartland — one of the flattest, most uniform landscapes in the country.
nature.climate_signature: Humid temperate climate — green fields, open horizon-to-horizon farmland, a much gentler climate than Patagonia's wind-blasted steppe or the northwest's high desert.

vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Heaviest concentration of the country's vehicle fleet given Buenos Aires' population.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Gen 3 with the distinctive black Google car; some Gen 4 in central Buenos Aires.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: The densest, most complete coverage in the country, concentrated in and around Buenos Aires and the agricultural Pampas road network.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same Río de la Plata cultural region, nearly identical flat grassland terrain, shared Rioplatense Spanish
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Uruguay's plates and bollards trend whiter overall without Argentina's darker plate center; Uruguay's Google car front is more consistently pale/ghostly than Argentina's black car.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same script and plate style
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The Pampas is flat green farmland with a mild humid climate; Patagonia is dry windswept steppe, and the northwest is high-altitude colourful desert — both look nothing like the Pampas.
